## Objective

This page summarizes a preliminary real-data exploration of the two-trait
MIRAGE extension using autism as trait 1 and schizophrenia as trait 2.

The goal is not to present a finalized association analysis. Instead, the goal
is to test whether the two public summary VCFs can be converted into a common
variant-level input matrix, whether joint MIRAGE can run on the resulting data,
and whether the top-ranked genes agree with external knowledge.

## Data Sources

Trait 1 uses the Autism Sequencing Consortium (ASC) summary VCF. Trait 2 uses
the SCHEMA schizophrenia summary VCF.

The analysis uses summary allele counts only:

| Trait | Case count field | Control count field | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASC autism | `ac_case` | `ac_ctrl` | Array-valued fields were summed over entries with `in_analysis=1`. |
| SCHEMA schizophrenia | `ac_case` | `ac_ctrl` | Only variants with `in_analysis=1` were used. |

De novo counts were not used. For SCHEMA, the `n_de_novo` field was ignored.

## Variant Groups

Both traits were mapped to the same six annotation groups used in the original
MIRAGE ASD analysis:

| Group | Definition |
|---|---|
| LoF, low LOEUF | Loss-of-function variant in a gene with LOEUF decile 1 |
| LoF, medium LOEUF | Loss-of-function variant in a gene with LOEUF decile 2-3 |
| LoF, high LOEUF | Loss-of-function variant in a gene with LOEUF decile 4-10 |
| Missense, high MPC | Missense variant with `MPC >= 2` |
| Missense, medium MPC | Missense variant with `1 <= MPC < 2` |
| Missense, low MPC | Missense variant with `MPC < 1` |

LOEUF deciles were assigned from the gnomAD v2.1.1 gene constraint table. The
ASC and SCHEMA VCFs contain `consequence` and `mpc`, but not a direct gnomAD
allele-frequency field. The working rare-variant filter therefore used the
within-cohort pooled allele frequency, `AF <= 0.1%`.

## Variant Overlap

The correct joint input uses the union of variant indices, not only shared
variants. A variant index is defined as:

```text
chromosome + position + reference allele + alternate allele
```

If a variant appears only in ASC, its SCHEMA case/control counts are set to
zero. If a variant appears only in SCHEMA, its ASC case/control counts are set
to zero.

Using only the exact variant intersection would discard nearly all rare
variants.

| Quantity | Count |
|---|---:|
| ASC variants after filtering | 406,842 |
| SCHEMA variants after filtering | 686,383 |
| Union variant indices | 1,093,122 |
| Exact shared variant indices | 103 |
| ASC genes | 17,581 |
| SCHEMA genes | 18,009 |
| Shared genes | 16,560 |

| Denominator | Exact variant overlap |
|---|---:|
| Shared variants / ASC variants | 0.025% |
| Shared variants / SCHEMA variants | 0.015% |

This is expected for rare variants: two studies may implicate the same gene
while observing different rare variants within that gene.

## Initial Joint MIRAGE Run

The first joint run used all six annotation groups and estimated the four
gene-state proportions freely.

| State | Estimate | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| `pi00` | 0.358 | Neither trait |
| `pi10` | 0.003 | Autism only |
| `pi01` | 0.408 | Schizophrenia only |
| `pi11` | 0.231 | Shared autism-schizophrenia risk |

This run recovered highly plausible autism genes, but the schizophrenia signal
was too broad.

| Criterion | Number of genes |
|---|---:|
| Autism posterior probability > 0.8 | 25 |
| SCHEMA posterior probability > 0.8 | 3,379 |
| Shared posterior probability > 0.8 | 25 |

The top autism genes were strongly concordant with known autism-risk genes.
Among the top 25 autism genes, 22 were SFARI score-1 genes.

| Rank | Gene | Autism PP | SCHEMA PP | Shared PP | SFARI score |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | SCN2A | 0.999 | 1.000 | 0.999 | 1 |
| 2 | POGZ | 0.997 | 0.998 | 0.995 | 1 |
| 3 | ADNP | 0.996 | 1.000 | 0.996 | 1 |
| 4 | CHD8 | 0.985 | 0.970 | 0.963 | 1 |
| 5 | SYNGAP1 | 0.983 | 0.991 | 0.978 | 1 |
| 6 | DYNC1H1 | 0.982 | 1.000 | 0.982 | 1 |
| 7 | GRIN2B | 0.973 | 0.981 | 0.964 | 1 |
| 8 | DYRK1A | 0.963 | 0.963 | 0.945 | 1 |
| 9 | SHANK3 | 0.952 | 1.000 | 0.952 | 1 |
| 10 | ANKRD11 | 0.952 | 0.999 | 0.951 | 1 |

The SCHEMA ranking also contained several known schizophrenia exome genes, but
the number of high-posterior SCHEMA genes was too large for a credible final
gene-discovery claim.

## Separate MIRAGE Diagnostic

To determine whether the broad SCHEMA signal came from the joint layer or from
the single-trait SCHEMA likelihood, separate MIRAGE fits were run for each
trait.

| Trait | Estimated risk-gene proportion | Genes with PP > 0.8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| ASC autism | 0.225 | 16 |
| SCHEMA schizophrenia | 0.639 | 3,375 |

This shows that the broad SCHEMA signal is already present in the separate
single-trait analysis. It is not created mainly by the joint shared state.

The likely explanation is calibration: SCHEMA has many more observed variants
and much larger allele numbers than ASC, and the six broad annotation groups
allow background burden to be interpreted as widespread risk-gene signal.

## Calibration Exploration

Two simple calibration strategies were explored.

First, the SCHEMA single-trait risk-gene proportion was fixed to sparse values
instead of being freely estimated. Second, the variant set was restricted to the
three strongest annotation groups:

```text
LoF, LOEUF decile 1
LoF, LOEUF decile 2-3
Missense, MPC >= 2
```

### SCHEMA Separate Fits

| Setting | SCHEMA variants | Risk-gene proportion | Genes with PP > 0.8 | Known SCZ genes in top 25 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Six groups, free delta | 686,383 | 0.639 | 3,375 | 5 |
| Six groups, fixed delta 0.01 | 686,383 | 0.010 | 163 | 7 |
| Six groups, fixed delta 0.03 | 686,383 | 0.030 | 278 | 7 |
| Six groups, fixed delta 0.05 | 686,383 | 0.050 | 367 | 7 |
| Six groups, fixed delta 0.10 | 686,383 | 0.100 | 540 | 7 |
| Strict three groups, free delta | 210,250 | 0.468 | 800 | 6 |
| Strict three groups, fixed delta 0.01 | 210,250 | 0.010 | 98 | 8 |
| Strict three groups, fixed delta 0.03 | 210,250 | 0.030 | 136 | 7 |
| Strict three groups, fixed delta 0.05 | 210,250 | 0.050 | 176 | 7 |
| Strict three groups, fixed delta 0.10 | 210,250 | 0.100 | 259 | 7 |

### Joint Fits

The sparse fixed prior used:

```text
pi00 = 0.94
pi10 = 0.02
pi01 = 0.03
pi11 = 0.01
```

This prior is sparse at the gene-state level. It means that most genes are
assumed a priori to be null, with smaller prior mass assigned to autism-only,
schizophrenia-only, and shared-risk states.

| Joint setting | ASC variants | SCHEMA variants | `pi00` | `pi10` | `pi01` | `pi11` | Autism PP > 0.8 | SCHEMA PP > 0.8 | Shared PP > 0.8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Six groups, free pi | 406,842 | 686,383 | 0.358 | 0.003 | 0.408 | 0.231 | 25 | 3,379 | 25 |
| Six groups, fixed sparse pi | 406,842 | 686,383 | 0.940 | 0.020 | 0.030 | 0.010 | 8 | 329 | 6 |
| Strict three groups, free pi | 16,161 | 210,250 | 0.504 | 0.029 | 0.263 | 0.204 | 26 | 795 | 24 |
| Strict three groups, fixed sparse pi | 16,161 | 210,250 | 0.940 | 0.020 | 0.030 | 0.010 | 9 | 166 | 8 |

The strict three-group plus sparse-prior analysis gives the cleanest
preliminary result: the schizophrenia list contracts substantially while the
top autism and schizophrenia genes remain enriched for known biology.

## External Validation

Autism genes were compared with the SFARI gene-scoring database. SFARI score 1
genes were treated as high-confidence autism-risk genes for this exploratory
check.

Schizophrenia genes were compared with published SCHEMA exome-significant genes:

```text
SETD1A, CUL1, XPO7, TRIO, CACNA1G, SP4, GRIA3, GRIN2A,
HERC1, RB1CC1, STAG1, ZNF136
```

The first ten genes come from the SCHEMA exome-sequencing study; STAG1 and
ZNF136 were added from the later SCHEMA expansion.

| Analysis | Top-25 validation result |
|---|---:|
| Six-group joint autism ranking vs. SFARI score 1 | 22 / 25 |
| Strict three-group joint autism ranking vs. SFARI score 1 | 21 / 25 |
| Six-group joint SCHEMA ranking vs. known SCZ genes | 5 / 25 |
| Strict three-group joint SCHEMA ranking vs. known SCZ genes | 5 / 25 |
| Strict three-group, sparse-prior joint SCHEMA ranking vs. known SCZ genes | 7 / 25 |

## Interpretation

This exploration supports three practical conclusions.

First, ASC and SCHEMA should be joined by the union of variant indices rather
than by the exact variant intersection. Exact rare-variant overlap is almost
zero, but gene-level overlap is high.

Second, the autism signal is robust and biologically credible. The top autism
genes are highly enriched for SFARI score-1 genes.

Third, SCHEMA requires calibration. With freely estimated gene-risk proportions,
the model assigns high posterior probability to too many schizophrenia genes.
Using a stricter damaging-variant set and a sparse gene-state prior gives a more
interpretable result while retaining known schizophrenia genes near the top.

## Current Recommendation

The most useful real-data analysis setting for continued development is:

```text
Trait 1: ASC autism
Trait 2: SCHEMA schizophrenia
Variant input: union variant index
Variant groups: strict three groups
Gene-state prior: sparse fixed pi
```

This should be treated as a preliminary calibrated real-data exploration, not
as a finalized discovery analysis.
